sources.entry: escrcpy -📱 Graphical Scrcpy to display and control Android devices, powered by Electron.[![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/viarotel-org/escrcpy) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Escrcpy is a graphical Electron desktop app that displays and controls Android devices using scrcpy.
summary.what_it_does: Escrcpy wraps scrcpy in a graphical interface for mirroring and controlling Android devices. Its README describes an embedded mirror window that auto-fits screen resolution and orientation, keyboard mapping for touch, joystick, swipe, scroll and automation, and a multi-device mode that controls several devices in one window with broadcast input, batch screenshots and APK install. It also lists a draggable control bar (rotation, screenshot, apps, files, terminal, AI assistant, automation), an AI "Copilot" built on MCP, visual automation scripts with screen image recognition, wireless ADB with LAN discovery, Gnirehtet reverse tethering, and customizable global hotkeys. The README notes that some advanced features come from a private extension repository, EscrcpyX, offered on a paid basis.
use_cases: Mirror and control an Android phone from a desktop computer
Control several Android devices at once from one window
Batch take screenshots or install APKs across multiple devices
Connect to an Android device over Wi-Fi with ADB
Automate repetitive taps and steps on Android devices
Share phone reverse tethering with a computer via Gnirehtet
how_to_run: Download a packaged release from the Releases Page
On macOS, install via Homebrew using the homebrew-escrcpy tap referenced in the README
For development, follow the Development Documentation referenced in the README
notable: Multi-device control in a single window with broadcast input
Keyboard mapping configured directly on the embedded mirror
AI Copilot built on MCP protocol with multi-model chat
Visual step-by-step automation with screen image recognition
Wireless ADB with LAN auto-discovery and Gnirehtet reverse tethering
caveats: Some advanced features come from the private EscrcpyX extension, offered on a paid basis
Support is limited and updates are irregular, per the README
Installation paths are release packages or Homebrew on macOS; the README names no other platforms
